issues.legal_issue: The statutory terms “son or daughter” in a female vendor’s pre-emption priority include only legitimate children unless the statute expressly or contextually gives them a broader meaning.
material_facts: The vendor sold agricultural land to the respondents, and her illegitimate son and daughter sued to pre-empt the sale.
The lower courts granted the appellants a limited decree, but the High Court dismissed the suit because they were not within the class entitled to pre-emption.
The statutory provision used “son or daughter” elsewhere for a male vendor and referred to a brother’s son in provisions concerning a female vendor.
The provision contained no express extension of “son or daughter” to include illegitimate children, and its context did not support that extension.
issues.conclusion: The terms “son or daughter” in the relevant provision mean only the legitimate son or daughter of the female vendor. The appellants were therefore not entitled to pre-emption, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The ordinary statutory meaning of “child,” “son,” or “daughter” includes legitimate children only. A broader meaning may follow from an express statutory definition or from context, but neither applied here. The repeated use of these terms in the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, as amended, supported a consistent meaning; the reference to a brother’s son likewise did not encompass an illegitimate son. The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, including its section 3(j) definition as an example of an express extension, did not determine the meaning of the pre-emption provision: statutory pre-emption rights could not be made to depend on the vendor’s religion or the personal law governing intestate succession. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.preemption_right_claim: A person claims a statutory priority to purchase property by bringing a pre-emption proceeding.
predicates.son_daughter_terms_recur: The governing statutory scheme uses the terms “son” or “daughter” repeatedly for persons with priority rights.
predicates.no_express_extension_to_illegitimate_chi: The governing statute does not expressly extend the relevant terms to illegitimate children.
predicates.context_does_not_expand_relationship_ter: The statutory context does not indicate that the relevant relationship terms include illegitimate children.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption claim depends on recurring statutory terms for children, and neither an express extension nor the context broadens those terms, illegitimate children are excluded from the statutory priority.
